newsitem.title: CHINA: China state firms asset-liability ratio 85 pct.
newsitem.headline: China state firms asset-liability ratio 85 pct.

text.p: The asset-liability ratio of China's 148,000 state-owned enterprises reached 85 percent at the end of 1995, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
Their debt owed to banks totalled 3.36 trillion yuan ($405 billion) -- higher than total personal bank deposits in China's banks of 2.97 trillion yuan ($358 billion), the newspaper said.
Each year, China's state firms must spend 100 billion yuan ($12 billion) in interest payments alone, it said.
The excessive borrowing has soared since China started to reform state firms in the early 1980s and shifted its system of budget subsidies to one by which firms had to turn to banks for credits.
Many firms, unable to find other sources of capital, relied on debt to operate, the newspaper said.
China says about one-third of its state firms are in the red while about another one-third are making losses.
